prompts.text: What is a first impression people often get wrong about you?
Would you rather someone ask a direct question or circle around a sensitive topic politely?
We discover within ten minutes that we strongly disagree on something important. What keeps the conversation worth having?
Small talk is useful only when it leads somewhere more honest. Agree or disagree?
What question helps you decide whether someone is genuinely curious or merely being polite?
Tell me about a time a stranger's honesty completely changed the direction of your day.
Which subject do you avoid with new people because it reveals too much too quickly?
A confident introduction can be warm without being impressive. What makes that possible?
Would you rather be remembered as unusually honest or unexpectedly kind?
Someone you just met corrects you in front of others. How do you decide whether to appreciate it or push back?
Which unpopular opinion are you willing to explain rather than defend?
People reveal more through the questions they avoid than the answers they give. What's your verdict?
When did an awkward first conversation turn into a relationship you valued?
What is one assumption you never want a new acquaintance to make on your behalf?
We have five minutes before going separate ways. Do you ask one meaningful question or trade contact details first?
A new acquaintance starts sharing gossip about a mutual friend. How do you stop the conversation without creating a scene?
How quickly should someone earn the right to challenge your opinion?
Being easy to talk to is not the same as being entitled to personal details. Agree?
Which compliment from someone new would make you suspicious rather than pleased?
You realise you have forgotten the name of someone who clearly remembers yours. What do you say?
Tell me about a time you trusted your first instinct about someone and were completely wrong.
Would you rather meet someone who challenges your thinking or someone who immediately understands your humour?
What personal question are you comfortable answering only when someone explains why they are asking?
A polished introduction can hide more than a clumsy one. Do you agree?
Someone new makes a joke that crosses your line, then says they were testing your sense of humour. How do you respond?
What is the fastest respectful way for a new person to lose your trust?
Describe a conversation with someone new that made you reconsider an old opinion.
Direct eye contact or an unexpectedly thoughtful question: which makes a stronger introduction?
What would make you leave a conversation even if doing so seemed impolite?
New connections need boundaries before they need vulnerability. Thoughts?
We are seated together at an event where neither of us knows anyone. What truth would make the situation less awkward?
What trait do you notice early because experience taught you not to ignore it?
Would you rather risk seeming too serious or risk leaving a meaningful question unasked?
A person you just met asks for a favour that would take an entire afternoon. What determines your answer?
Which version of honesty feels rude from a stranger but caring from a close friend?
You can respect someone's boundaries without understanding them. Agree or disagree?
Tell me about a time you decided not to pursue a promising new connection. What did you notice?
Someone new shares a vulnerable story and asks you to keep it private. What response shows care without promising too much?
How do you tell the difference between someone being confidently curious and deliberately provocative?
Would you rather know immediately that someone dislikes you or discover later that they were pretending?
People who are comfortable saying 'I don't know' are easier to trust. Have you found that?
You overhear someone you just met taking credit for another person's idea. Do you challenge it, ask a question, or stay out?
What is one value you prefer to state clearly rather than let people discover slowly?
Tell me about a stranger who made you feel respected without trying to impress you.
A candid answer with an awkward pause or a smooth answer that says very little?
What do you listen for when someone describes a person who is not present?
You and a new acquaintance both want the same limited opportunity. How would you compete without damaging mutual respect?
Chemistry can make people overlook incompatibility before they know each other well. Agree?
What would you disclose first if the goal were to skip the performance and meet honestly?
A new person says, 'Trust me,' before giving you any reason to. What would you need to see next?
